messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Analyse diffmeth with More than two treatment
messages.body_plain:
You can use reorganize() function on methlyBase or methylRawList objects to get the specific pairs you want and then run calculateDiffMeth. You can also specify a new treatment vector when using reorganize.

Best
Altuna

Here is using the datasets of the vignette

file.list=list( system.file("extdata", "test1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                 system.file("extdata", "test2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                 system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                 system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit") )

myobj=methRead( file.list, sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),assembly="hg18",treatment=c(1,1,0,0))

filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL,
                                      hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

meth=unite(myobj, destrand=TRUE,min.per.group=1L)

myDiffFiltered = getMethylDiff(myDiff)

gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures(system.file("extdata", "refseq.hg18.bed.txt",
                                           package = "methylKit"))
promoters=regionCounts(myobj,gene.obj$promoters)

percentcoverage = length(subsetByOverlaps(gene.obj$promoters,as(meth,"GRanges")))*100/length(gene.obj$promoters)

messages.subject: Overdispersion: F Test or Chisq Test
messages.subject_clean: Overdispersion: F Test or Chisq Test
messages.body_plain:
Hi Altuna,

Is there a consensus on whether to use the F-Test or Chisq-Test when correction for overdispersion during calculateDiffMeth? I see from the vignette that F-test is the default when correcting for overdispersion but the Chisq-test can also be specified. I was wondering if F-test should strictly be used since that is the default, and in what cases one could use the Chisq-test.

Thanks for your help,

Brett

messages.subject: Correct for batch effect with covariate logistic regression in Methylkit
messages.subject_clean: Correct for batch effect with covariate logistic regression in Methylkit
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

am doing differentially methylation analysis and I have 5 samples:

2 (wt) Vs 3 (treatment)

the problem is that one of my wild type clone was sequenced in a different day (even if in the same machine). Even if the methylation values Pearson correlation is very high among the 2 wild type (0.91), I would like to distinguish this before running DMRs estimation. My question is:

is it possible to use the logistic regression model with covariate in DMR analysis? So that in my script I will have:

file.list <- list("control1.myCpG.gz","control2.myCpG.gz","test1.myCpG.gz","test2.myCpG.gz","test3.myCpG.gz")
myobj=readBismarkCytosineReport(file.list,sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("ctrl1","ctrl2","test1","test2","test3"),assembly="mm10",treatment=c(0,0,1,1,1))
tiles <- tileMethylCounts(myobj,cov.bases = 2, win.size = 250,step.size = 250)
meth=unite(tiles,destrand=FALSE)
covariate=data.frame(experiment=c(0,1,0,0,0)) #here the covariate
myDiff <- calculateDiffMeth(meth,covariates=covariates,overdispersion=c("MN"),effect=c("predicted"),test=c("F"),num.cores=4)

I have checked some of the DMRs and I have realized that in all the estimated the two wild-type look very similar, so there is not a trend towards estimate DMRs in which the differences in the variability between control and treatment is mainly due to the clone sequenced in another round. Also, the estimated DMRs in which the differences between the control and treatment are due just by one of the two clones are discarded.

Is it correct to operate in such way?

Am looking forward to your comment and suggestion.
Best regards

messages.subject: Help in better understanding destrand=TRUE
messages.body_plain:
meth=unite(myobj,destrand=TRUE)

According to the methylkit vignette:
Setting destrand=TRUE (the default is FALSE) will merge reads on both strands of a CpG dinucleotide. This provides better coverage, but only advised when looking at CpG methylation

I am not sure what are the recommendations when you are using this meth object for downstream analysis such as finding DMR (with the eDMR package) or when you are annotating it with gene objects. If you take into consideration the strand information there might be some changes in the annotation.

I can illustrate this with an example:
Lets suppose regionX where the DMCs are found (in the forward strand only) is close to 2 genes  :
1)GENE.A in the + strand
2) GENE.B in the - strand

Now if we put destrand=TRUE and then we annotate this DMC it be assigned to GENE.B since this is the gene closes to it. But if we consider the strand orientation with destrand=FALSE  it will be assigned to GENE.A .

       5'----------------regionX(w/DMCs)------------------------------GENE.A-----3'>>>>    [+]
<<<3'GENE.B-----regionX------------------------------------------------------------5'             [-]

I would say in reality most CpGs islands/promoters are methylated or not in both strands so this should not mater, but what about the hemi-methylated regions? eg imprinted genes or de-novo methylated regions.... What are the rules to follow, is it safe to place destrand=TRUE and make the assumption that the CpGs will be DMC are the same in both strands?

Good afternoon,

I am doing analyses with methylkit using the following functions:

filtered.obj <- filterByCoverage(obj,lo.count = 3,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

filtered.obj <- unite(filtered.obj, destrand=TRUE)

I obtain a methylBase object with 321902 rows. However, my individuals *_CpG.txt files' have around 20 million lines of C's. I decided to make a join of all the files from the nine individuals and it turn out that they have more than 7 million positions in common (the intersection of the nine of them), all of them with a coverage higher than 3 in every individual. Why am I getting a methylBase object with only 300 thousand positions? Or am I understanding things in the wrong way?

Thanks a lot in advance.

Begoña

Hi, Altuna,

Thanks for your answer. I have made smaller toy datasets *_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt (with just 500,000 lines, header included) and redone the analyses. Those files are 27 Kb. Are those the kind of example files that you would want me to send? How could I send them to you?

I explain below how I proceeded with them to be sure of the number of lines they share. Please let me know if my explanations are not clear enough.

So, I am using these toy datasets with 500,000 lines. My datasets *_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt are like follow (there are nine of them). They are sorted after the first column, the chrBase:

#Structure of my CpG files:
chrBase    chr    base    strand    coverage    freqC    freqT

lp23.s00001.10000387    lp23.s00001    10000387    F    12    66.67    33.33
lp23.s00001.10000388    lp23.s00001    10000388    R    10    90.00    10.00

To estimate the number of common positions to my nine individuals, I made a join:

join Ll002_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt Ll003_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Ll019_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Ll107_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Ll108_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Ll109_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Lp0325_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Lp0735_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt | join - Lp0738_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt > Ll_Lp_intergenic_sorted_toy_join.txt

The output file, Ll_Lp_intergenic_sorted_toy_join.txt, has 163,303 lines (from the initial 500,000 I had in every individual file at the start)

What I did to be re-assure that all those positions are common among all individuals:
I counted the number of times a "p" (from the expression  "lp23") appears per line. It appears 10 times in all of them, but the header:

 >tr -d -c 'p\n' < Ll_Lp_intergenic_sorted_toy_join.txt | awk '{ print length; }' | grep "10" | wc -l
 >163302
I thus understand that all individuals have these positions.

Then I ran methylkit:
R
library(methylKit)
file.list=list("Ll002_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Ll003_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Ll019_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Ll107_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Ll108_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Ll109_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Lp0325_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Lp0735_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt","Lp0738_CpG_intergenic_sorted_toy.txt")
intergenic_sorted_toy <- methRead(file.list,sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("Ll002","Ll003","Ll019","Ll107","Ll108","Ll109","Lp0325","Lp0735","Lp0738"),
assembly="lp23",context="CpG",treatment=c(0,0,0,0,0,0,1,1,1))

filtered.intergenic_sorted_toy <- filterByCoverage(intergenic_sorted_toy,lo.count = 5,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

filtered.intergenic_sorted_toy <- unite(filtered.intergenic_sorted_toy, destrand=TRUE)

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I want use this readBismarkCytosineReport function but after running :
devtools::source_gist("4839e615e2401d73fe51")

Error in r_files[[which]] : invalid subscript type 'closure'

How can I fix it?

Thanks

On Wednesday, June 1, 2016 at 6:45:27 PM UTC+4:30, avil...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
>
> This is a question about generating a straightforward standard pipeline from bismark sample-by-sample CpG counting directly into methylKit multi-sample DMR calling.
>
> The methylkit authors kindly provided a loading mechanism for the .CpG_report.txt.gz file from bismark, which means that on a pipeline setup (e.g. Galaxy or Dnanexus), one can go from bismark methylation extractor output directly loaded into methylkit, without intermediate files.
>
> Find below the code snippet with the solution (assumes 2 cases and 2 controls, and min.cov=10).
>
> Feedback welcomed:
>
> $ Rscript run_methylkit_four_samples.R CASE1.CpG_report.txt.gz CASE2.CpG_report.txt.gz CONTROL1.CpG_report.txt.gz CONTROL2.CpG_report.txt.gz 10
>
>
> ########
>
> #!/usr/bin/Rscript
>
> thisdir = getwd()
> tempdir <- function() thisdir
> unlockBinding("tempdir", baseenv())
> assignInNamespace("tempdir", tempdir, ns="base", envir=baseenv())
> assign("tempdir", tempdir, baseenv())
> lockBinding("tempdir", baseenv())
>
> library(methylKit)
> library(tools)
> args<-commandArgs(TRUE)
>
> # readBismarkCytosineReport function
> devtools::source_gist("4839e615e2401d73fe51")
>
> file.list = list(args[1],args[2],args[3],args[4])
>
> # This reads straight from the output of bismark, works for both strands
> myobj = readBismarkCytosineReport(
>         file.list,
>           sample.id <http://sample.id>=list(
>   	  strsplit(basename(args[1]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
>           strsplit(basename(args[2]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
>   	  strsplit(basename(args[3]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
>   	  strsplit(basename(args[4]), '[_]')[[1]][1]
>   	       ),
>   	assembly="hg38",
>   	treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
>   	min.cov=args[5])
>
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample01.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[1]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample02.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[2]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample03.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[3]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample04.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[4]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
>
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample01.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[1]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample02.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[2]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample03.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[3]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample04.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[4]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
>
> meth = unite(myobj)
> pdf(file="Methylkit.02.Meth_CorrelationPlot.pdf",width=12,height=12); getCorrelation(meth,plot=T); dev.off()
>
> # cluster all samples using correlation distance and return a tree object for plclust
> hc = clusterSamples(meth, dist="correlation", method="ward", plot=FALSE)
>
> # cluster all samples using correlation distance and plot hiarachical clustering
> pdf(file="Methylkit.03.PCASamples.ctreeplot.pdf",width=12,height=12); clusterSamples(meth, dist="correlation", method="ward", plot=TRUE); dev.off()
>
> # screeplot of principal component analysis.
> pdf(file="Methylkit.03.PCASamples.screeplot.pdf",width=12,height=12); PCASamples(meth, screeplot=TRUE); dev.off()
>
> # principal component anlaysis of all samples.
> pdf(file="Methylkit.03.PCASamples.pcaxyplot.pdf",width=12,height=12); PCASamples(meth); dev.off()
>
> myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
> write.table(myDiff, file="Methylkit.04.DiffMeth.tsv", sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
> myDiff25p.hyper = get.methylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01,type="hyper")
> write.table(myDiff25p.hyper,"Methylkit.04.hyper_methylated.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
> myDiff25p.hypo = get.methylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01,type="hypo")
> write.table(myDiff25p.hypo,"Methylkit.04.hypo_methylated.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
> myDiff25p = get.methylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01)
> write.table(myDiff25p,"Methylkit.04.differentialy_methylated.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
> pdf("Methylkit.04.DiffMethPerChr.pdf",width=12,height=12); diffMethPerChr(myDiff,plot=TRUE,qvalue.cutoff=0.01,meth.cutoff=25); dev.off()
>
> gene.obj=read.transcript.features("/Annotations/UCSC_database/refseq.hg38.bed.txt")
>
> diffAnn = annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p, gene.obj)
> write.table(getAssociationWithTSS(diffAnn),"Methylkit.05.AssociationWithTSS.txt", sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
>
> pdf("Methylkit.05.TargetAnnotation.piechart1.pdf",width=12,height=12); plotTargetAnnotation(diffAnn, precedence = TRUE, main ="differential methylation annotation"); dev.off()
>
> write.table(getFeatsWithTargetsStats(diffAnn, percentage = TRUE),"Methylkit.05.FeatsWithStargetsStats.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
>
> tmpfiles <- dir(path=getwd(), pattern="*.CpG_report.txt")

messages.subject: Question dmc analysis
messages.body_plain:
I have a little question about dmc analysis.
If a have a control sample as:
Chromosome 894 - 34 181 0.15814 CHG 2.07E-55 2.15E-53
Chromosome 895 + 44 161 0.214634 CHG 1.32E-77 4.16E-75
Chromosome 1866 - 14 95 0.12844 CHG 2.27E-22 1.03E-20
Chromosome 1998 + 32 161 0.165803 CHG 5.89E-53 5.54E-51
Chromosome 2041 - 31 115 0.212329 CHG 5.33E-55 5.45E-53
Chromosome 2339 - 23 120 0.160839 CHG 3.51E-38 2.02E-36
Chromosome 2612 + 25 122 0.170068 CHG 5.10E-42 3.26E-40

And treatment  sample as:
Chromosome 894 - 17 181 0.0858586 CHG 4.58E-24 8.34E-22
Chromosome 895 + 10 160 0.0588235 CHG 4.37E-13 2.64E-11
Chromosome 2041 - 10 132 0.0704225 CHG 7.13E-14 4.55E-12
Chromosome 2339 - 11 164 0.0628571 CHG 1.42E-14 9.51E-13
Chromosome 2612 + 16 145 0.0993789 CHG 8.75E-24 1.54E-21

As you see, site 1866 and 1998 are only detected to be methylated in the control sample.
When I use the unite command to merge the data, these two sites are not included in the merged data, since they only existed in the control sample. And then they will not appear in the final dmc result.
Is there a way that I could make sites like this also be included?

I have tried to firstly mark both samples as control, merge them with min.per.group=1L, and the reorganize. But I got error as there are NAs in the merged data.

Thanks!

Zixi Chen

messages.body_plain:
from the methRead help:
Bismark aligner can output methylation information per base in multiple formats. With pipeline='bismarkCoverage', the function reads bismark coverage files, which have chr,start,end, number of cytosines (methylated bases) and number of thymines (unmethylated bases) format. If bismark coverage files are used the function will not have the strand information,so beware of that fact. With pipeline='bismarkCytosineReport', the function expects cytosine report files from Bismark, which have chr,start, strand, number of cytosines (methylated bases) , number of thymines (unmethylated bases),context and trinucletide context format.

> > > >
> > > > Find below the code snippet with the solution (assumes 2 cases and 2 controls, and min.cov=10).

> > > > Feedback welcomed:

> > > >
> > > >
> > > > ########
> > > >
> > > > #!/usr/bin/Rscript
> > > >
> > > > thisdir = getwd()

> > > >
> > > > library(methylKit)
> > > > library(tools)
> > > > args<-commandArgs(TRUE)
> > > >
> > > > # readBismarkCytosineReport function

> > > >
> > > > file.list = list(args[1],args[2],args[3],args[4])
> > > >
> > > > # This reads straight from the output of bismark, works for both strands
> > > > myobj = readBismarkCytosineReport(
> > > >         file.list,
> > > >           sample.id <http://sample.id>=list(
> > > >   	  strsplit(basename(args[1]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
> > > >           strsplit(basename(args[2]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
> > > >   	  strsplit(basename(args[3]), '[_]')[[1]][1],
> > > >   	  strsplit(basename(args[4]), '[_]')[[1]][1]
> > > >   	       ),
> > > >   	assembly="hg38",
> > > >   	treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
> > > >   	min.cov=args[5])
> > > >
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample01.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[1]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample02.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[2]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample03.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[3]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.MethylationStats.Sample04.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getMethylationStats(myobj[[4]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> > > >
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample01.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[1]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()

> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample03.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[3]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.01.CoverageStats.Sample04.pdf",width=12,height=12) ; getCoverageStats(myobj[[4]],plot=T,both.strands=T); dev.off()

> > > > meth = unite(myobj)

> > > >
> > > > # principal component anlaysis of all samples.
> > > > pdf(file="Methylkit.03.PCASamples.pcaxyplot.pdf",width=12,height=12); PCASamples(meth); dev.off()
> > > >
> > > > myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
> > > > write.table(myDiff, file="Methylkit.04.DiffMeth.tsv", sep='\t', quote=FALSE)
> > > > myDiff25p.hyper = get.methylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01,type="hyper")
> > > > write.table(myDiff25p.hyper,"Methylkit.04.hyper_methylated.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)

> > > > write.table(myDiff25p.hypo,"Methylkit.04.hypo_methylated.txt",sep='\t', quote=FALSE)

> > > >

messages.subject: diffmeth different results between MethylKit v0.99 and latest (1.5)
messages.subject_clean: diffmeth different results between MethylKit v0.99 and latest (1.5)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I have run some RRBS samples (3 controls vs 3 treated, paired), in two different installations; one of them with R 3.3 and MethylKit's version 0.99.4, and the other with R 3.4, in which MethylKit was updated to 1.3.8.
Using the exact same code, I got 75441 differentially methylated (padj<0.05) CpGs with the old version, and 21288 with the new. (If I skip the normalizeCoverage step, I get ~40K/~10K, so roughly half for both cases)
I noticed in the NEWS log, that there were indeed changes in the CalculateDiffMeth function:

"* changes to calculateDiffMeth() function: add a message explaining
  the calculation procedure based on either two or more treatment groups,
  fixed bugs that prohibited the use of treatment groups other than 0/1
  in two group case, allow for more than two groups, update tests"

Were there major changes in the tests that would explain such differences in the amount of significantly detected CpGs?

The code used in both tests was:

rrbs.file.list=list("file1.txt", "file2.txt", "file3.txt", "file4.txt", "file5.txt", "file6.txt" )
rrbs.myobj=methRead(rrbs.file.list, sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("1","2","3","4","5","6"),assembly="hg19",treatment=c(1,1,0,0,1,0), context="CpG")
rrbs.filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(rrbs.myobj, lo.count=10, lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=NULL, hi.perc=99.9)
rrbs.filtered.myobj2 = normalizeCoverage(rrbs.filtered.myobj)
rrbs.meth=unite(rrbs.filtered.myobj2, destrand=TRUE)
covariates=data.frame(patient=c("1", "2", "2", "1", "3", "3"))
diffmeth<-calculateDiffMeth(rrbs.meth,covariates=covariates,mc.cores=2, overdispersion="MN", test="Chisq")

Thanks!

messages.subject: A problem in gene annotation (CpG in gene body but not the nearest gene)
messages.subject_clean: A problem in gene annotation (CpG in gene body but not the nearest gene)
messages.body_plain:
Dear sir/madam,
When I get the differentially methylated CpG, I often annotated the site using getAssociationWithTSS. But I found a CpG site may be annotated to one gene with the nearest distance to TSS, while the CpG site may within the gene body of another gene which does not have the nearest distance to TSS. But I think in this situation, the gene body should be considered first, doesn't it? How to set the gene body first?

> it seems like v1.3 is more stringent, it could be that the overdispersion is not properly used in the earlier version either due to a bug or user error. >
> Best,
> Altuna

>
> On Wed, Nov 29, 2017 at 1:06 AM, Vicky Revuelta <revue...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I attach the diffmeth results for both. The results were obtained running the code that was mentioned in my original post in both systems (R3.3-methylKit 0.99 / R3.4-methylKit 1.3).
> > In any case, I'll stick to the newest version results, but my biggest concern is the magnitude of the difference between both runs.
> >
> >
> > ​
> >  MethylKitresults_v0-99.txt <https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tDwnZXptkhKmw2d2qLQeKYNbIPswazB4/view?usp=drive_web>

If you have more concerns please send a reproducible example. the example should include minimal data and code that shows the discrepancy between two sets of results. This could be obtained if you saved diffmeth results from both runs.
> > >
> > > Best,
> > > altuna
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Mon, Nov 27, 2017 at 10:45 PM, MVR <revue...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Hi,
> > > > I have run some RRBS samples (3 controls vs 3 treated, paired), in two different installations; one of them with R 3.3 and MethylKit's version 0.99.4, and the other with R 3.4, in which MethylKit was updated to 1.3.8.
> > > > Using the exact same code, I got 75441 differentially methylated (padj<0.05) CpGs with the old version, and 21288 with the new. (If I skip the normalizeCoverage step, I get ~40K/~10K, so roughly half for both cases)
> > > > I noticed in the NEWS log, that there were indeed changes in the CalculateDiffMeth function:
> > > >
> > > > "* changes to calculateDiffMeth() function: add a message explaining
> > > >   the calculation procedure based on either two or more treatment groups,
> > > >   fixed bugs that prohibited the use of treatment groups other than 0/1
> > > >   in two group case, allow for more than two groups, update tests"
> > > >
> > > > Were there major changes in the tests that would explain such differences in the amount of significantly detected CpGs?
> > > >
> > > > The code used in both tests was:
> > > >
> > > > rrbs.file.list=list("file1.txt", "file2.txt", "file3.txt", "file4.txt", "file5.txt", "file6.txt" )
> > > > rrbs.myobj=methRead(rrbs.file.list, sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("1","2","3","4","5","6"),assembly="hg19",treatment=c(1,1,0,0,1,0), context="CpG")
> > > > rrbs.filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(rrbs.myobj, lo.count=10, lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=NULL, hi.perc=99.9)
> > > > rrbs.filtered.myobj2 = normalizeCoverage(rrbs.filtered.myobj)
> > > > rrbs.meth=unite(rrbs.filtered.myobj2, destrand=TRUE)
> > > > covariates=data.frame(patient=c("1", "2", "2", "1", "3", "3"))
> > > > diffmeth<-calculateDiffMeth(rrbs.meth,covariates=covariates,mc.cores=2, overdispersion="MN", test="Chisq")
> > > >
> > > > Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
I can reproduce the latest version of methylKit results with these treatment and covariate vectors. But I couldn't find a way to reproduce the v0.99 results by varying parameters.

But changing the covariate vector between scripts will yield the same methylation difference but different p-values. And if you are not using a version control system strictly there is no way to tell if something has changed in your script between the v0.99 and the latest methylKit version.

Best,
Altuna
